previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including type 1 diabetes, pancreas transplant, end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis, chronic heart failure, and recent hospitalization for anemia and hypotension was readmitted for fatigue, weakness, and left leg swelling. She was found to have bilateral deep vein thromboses and was started on heparin. A stool test confirmed Clostridioides difficile infection, which was treated with oral vancomycin, leading to improvement in her fatigue and nausea. Her hemoglobin dropped transiently, requiring one unit of packed red blood cells, but remained stable thereafter. An MRI of the head showed no acute abnormalities, with findings consistent with chronic small vessel disease. Warfarin was restarted, and she was transitioned to extended care with plans for outpatient follow-up in nephrology, hematology, and primary care to manage ongoing anticoagulation, dialysis, and neurologic symptoms.

concerning for pulmonary edema. She had an echo showing an EF

and photophobia were concerning for worsening glaucoma vs. viral

underlying consolidation is difficult to exclude.  Patient is status post

right lung.  The patient is status post median sternotomy and cardiac valve
replacement.  Cardiac and mediastinal silhouettes are stable.

consolidation is difficult to exclude.

INDICATION:  Right IJ central venous line attempt.  Please evaluate for
pneumothorax.

FINDINGS:  No central venous line visualized.  No pneumothorax identified. 
Otherwise, stable examination with unchanged left base retrocardiac
opacification likely representing a combination of atelectasis and effusion. 
Cardiomediastinal and hilar contours are unchanged.

and might reflect need for dialysis.  Bilateral pleural effusions, right more

left lower lobe.  In the appropriate clinical setting, superimposed pneumonia
